annotations.text:
Roster grid: every client on one screen, problems sorted to the top.
The three things the spreadsheet can't show — trend direction, compliance %, and staleness — are the three columns that earn their place here.

Week banding is deliberate — it mirrors the merged WEEK column in your sheet, but each band now carries its own averages.
Missing days appear as inline rows rather than silent blanks.
Accent colour is a live control on each artboard (the chip above the frame) — lime, cyan, orange and violet are loaded. Nothing else in the palette changes.

A — EVIDENCE. Bets on proof. The hero is a real client's 16-week record, and the streak grid turns daily check-ins into the argument itself.
Strongest claim, no photography needed. Risk: abstract, and no human face anywhere.

B — PROTOCOL. Bets on seriousness. Reads like an engineering spec: mono type, hairline rules, a sample check-in record shown raw.
Deliberately anti-hype. Risk: cold, and it will not convert someone who wants warmth.

C — EDITORIAL. Bets on emotion. Serif display type, full-bleed portraiture, one big client quote.
Most immediately likeable. Risk: it needs real photography you may not have, and it is the most conventional of the three.
